text: AI can make you sound like an expert.
This is ProofPilot AI. Don't just trust AI. Verify it.
Here is a marketing post that an AI wrote in seconds. It is polished, it is confident, and it is full of facts: a company milestone, a launch date, a famous landmark, and a statistic.
But confident doesn't always mean correct. Which of these facts would survive a check?
So let's check it. This is the real ProofPilot app, recorded live, with nothing staged. We paste the draft, and select Check claims.
ProofPilot finds the factual claims and highlights them in place. Then it checks each claim against live web sources, and the verdicts arrive one by one.
And there it is. Two claims are supported. One is contradicted. One is unverified. The verdict at the top is clear: review before publishing.
Select the red claim. The Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye. ProofPilot shows the exact passage that contradicts the claim, with a link to the source.
Code confirms that every excerpt really is in the retrieved page, so a citation can never be invented.
The amber claim is a statistic with no reputable source. ProofPilot does not guess. It says: unverified.
And the green claims come with their evidence too. Transparency, not blind trust.
ProofPilot is for anyone who publishes with AI: professionals, students, researchers, and content creators. One wrong fact can cost your credibility.
So before you publish AI-generated content, check whether the facts can survive scrutiny.
ProofPilot AI. Look confident. Stay credible. Don't just trust AI. Verify it.
